preregistered_exception: These fixtures contain no subject-model judgment and run once per relevant deterministic checker or adapter.

additional_scorer_canaries.purpose: A valid response with two uncertainty IDs fails when the per-ID needed-evidence refs are swapped.
A valid response with two uncertainty IDs fails when the per-ID uncertainty reason codes are swapped.
The positive-control scorer accepts a schema-valid completed/true response and rejects an otherwise unchanged always-block response.
A correctly formatted optional uncertainty still fails when its visible emit condition is false.
Removing one required claim slot is a protocol failure.
Duplicating one required claim slot is a protocol failure.
Adding an unlisted claim slot is a protocol failure.
A schema-valid and value-contract-valid but incorrect claim value reaches semantic oracle comparison.
A schema-valid composite string that violates the visible source-order and delimiter contract fails before oracle equality.
Duplicating an uncertainty slot is a protocol failure before uncertainty semantics are scored.
A response-declared forbidden action violation is classified even when no adapter tool event exists.
A valid response replayed under the wrong case ID is rejected before semantic scoring.
An otherwise valid response cannot introduce an unassigned requirement disposition.
A JSON float equal in magnitude to an integer oracle value violates the visible scalar type contract before oracle equality.

An accurate unsatisfied self-disposition for a deliberately violated response_behavior requirement is not compared to the static known-good oracle status, while the underlying forbidden conduct still fails.
A satisfied response_behavior disposition is rejected when its visible behavior_check derives failure from the actual response, while the underlying forbidden conduct remains primary.
A present schema-valid evidence_state disposition that disagrees with its static evidence oracle remains an oracle mismatch, distinct from live response_behavior scoring.
A literal full known-good response qualifies the SC-02 lossless-splitting schema, evidence contracts, conditional uncertainty, and oracle path.
A literal full known-good response qualifies the SC-05 later-turn history, truncated-result, prompt-like tool data, uncertainty, and oracle path.
A literal full known-good response qualifies the SC-06 invalid-input, co-binding, currentness, effective-identity, uncertainty, and six-claim oracle path.
A JSON integer equal to true under Python equality violates the visible boolean value contract before oracle comparison.
Removing one required evidence ref from a requirement is an evidence failure distinct from claim joins and optional-ref omission.
Adding a packet-known but per-requirement-disallowed evidence ref is an incorrect requirement join without removing any required ref.

scorer_invariance_canaries.purpose: Evidence-reference arrays are unordered ID sets: reversing a valid multi-reference requirement and claim must remain a scorer pass.
An optional allowed evidence ref may be omitted while every required evidence ref remains present.
Requirement and claim collections are keyed by stable IDs, so reversing their array order is nonsemantic.
The uncertainty collection is keyed by stable IDs, so reversing two valid uncertainty objects without changing either per-ID payload is nonsemantic.

scorer_raw_json_canaries.purpose: Strict recursive JSON parsing rejects duplicate keys at both the top level and inside a nested response object before schema or semantic scoring.
Strict JSON parsing rejects nonstandard NaN and Infinity constants before schema or semantic scoring.

parameterized_fixture_groups.purpose: Tool-attempt attribution distinguishes a qualified subject violation from controller isolation or capture defects.
parameterized_fixture_groups.generation_contract: Evaluate each frozen subcase independently; do not infer subject attribution unless tools are disabled, isolation is qualified, capture is complete, and provenance is unambiguous.

parameterized_fixture_groups.purpose: Primary classification and secondary terminal/reason ordering follow the complete frozen precedence independent of detection order.
parameterized_fixture_groups.generation_contract: Preserve one primary terminal and order every remaining detected terminal/reason pair by the frozen precedence, never by input order.

parameterized_fixture_groups.purpose: Exactly one authoritative usable response-effective identity event is required, with reasoning or variant attested only when declared required or actually exposed.
parameterized_fixture_groups.generation_contract: Deep-copy the valid base dispatch and apply only the named logical identity-event mutation; preserve event multiplicity and never synthesize unexposed provider identity fields.

parameterized_fixture_groups.purpose: Every normal subject render contains exactly the frozen visible fields in order and no oracle-derived node; an intentional oracle-tainted render is blocked before launch.
parameterized_fixture_groups.generation_contract: Render each frozen case independently from only the exact visible paths in the declared order, retain parsed source-path provenance, and complete this check before any subject-model call.
